description: Powerful layer over OpenAI and Anthropic supporting chaining and recursion scenarios. Includes provider failover, a fluent SDK for chaining, templates, structured output, server-side code execution, and text processing. .NET 10 only.
releaseNotes:
5.1.1 fixes a retry gap on OpenAI. A transport fault - a refused connection, a reset socket, a DNS failure - reaches us as a ClientResultException carrying no status, because no response arrived to carry one. The provider decided retryability from that status, where neither 429 nor 5xx matches zero, so the failure most worth another attempt got exactly one, and no failover either. It now escapes to the retry policy, which reads the inner exception chain and already handles it. Behaviour on every other status is unchanged, and no API moved.

			5.1 adds the current models on both vendors and the two reasoning effort levels they introduced.

			Models. OpenAI gains Gpt_6_Astra, Gpt_5_6_Sol, Gpt_5_6_Terra and Gpt_5_6_Luna. Anthropic gains Claude_Fable_5_1 and Claude_Fable_5. Enum values are appended rather than renumbered, so anything persisting the underlying int is unaffected.

			Reasoning effort. OuroReasoningEffort gains XHigh and Max. Both providers accept them on their newer models and reject them on older ones, which fails the call rather than quietly serving a different level.

			Refusals. OuroStopReason gains Refusal, and IsComplete now reports false for it. Claude Fable 5.1 can decline a request with HTTP 200 and an empty answer; before this it read as a finished response that happened to say nothing.

			Ouroboros 5.0 removes the provider SDK from the public API and adds Anthropic alongside OpenAI. It is a breaking release: MIGRATION_4.4_to_5.0.md covers every change with before and after code, and ends in a checklist.

			Providers. Claude models route through the same client. Configure both keys via the OuroborosOptions overload of AddOuroboros and name the model on ChatOptions. Structured output, server-side code execution and file I/O all work on either provider from one ChatOptions, because the JSON schema is generated by Ouroboros rather than taken from a vendor SDK. The OpenAI path moved off Betalgo onto the official OpenAI package over the Responses API, which is invisible from calling code with two exceptions: ChatOptions.User is now ChatOptions.OpenAi.User, and StopSequences are refused on OpenAI because the Responses API has no stop parameter at all.

			Failover. Name fallback models per call with ChatOptions.FallbackModels, or once for the client with SetDefaultFallback, and a call the primary cannot serve is retried on the next model in the chain. Only transient failures move down it: a request the provider rejected on its merits fails where it stands, because it would fail identically on the next provider at twice the cost. A chain naming a provider you have no key for throws from AddOuroboros rather than during the outage. OnChatCompleted now fires once per attempt, so a consumer logging these writes one row per attempt, and ChatCompletedArgs gains Attempt, NextModel and Model. FAILOVER.md is the full description.

			Responses. OuroResponseSuccess.Content is the response broken into typed blocks, and StopReason with IsComplete make truncation visible - before this, a response cut off at the token ceiling was indistinguishable from a complete one, and truncated structured output silently parsed to a null ResponseObject. A Claude turn whose server-side tool loop pauses is now continued for you, with the blocks and token usage of every round folded into one response.

			Reliability. Per-attempt timeouts via ChatOptions.Timeout, a CancellationToken parameter on ChatAsync, and a retry policy that no longer retries timeouts. A throwing OnChatCompleted hook no longer fails the chat it was logging; choose what happens with OnChatCompletedFailure. ChatAsync works on a copy of your options, so a reused ChatOptions no longer carries the first call's model forever and no longer sends a stale structured-output schema. SetDefaultChatModel finally applies the reasoning effort it accepts, which it had silently discarded since 4.0.

			Surface. OuroClient implements IOuroClient, so you can mock it. Dialog.Messages exposes the conversation without reaching into internals. OuroClient.TokenCount now takes a model and uses the right encoding for it, so any counts you stored before 5.0 were wrong. The text-completions API, the ChatOptions sampling parameters and the NoType sentinel are gone. A conversation with no user or assistant turn is sent as system-role input on OpenAI and refused up front on Anthropic, whose API cannot express it; an empty message list is refused on both, naming the fix rather than passing along a vendor error.

			Dependencies. Betalgo and TypeMerger are both gone. The template engine builds its own render context now, which also means a global context passed as an ExpandoObject reaches the template instead of being silently dropped.
title: Ouroboros
